checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The opening pages build seduction through sensory ritual before any threat appears: Leaf's unteachable three-press rhythm on the heat-stone, glow-rats read like instruments, the blue bioluminescent Still pool described as giving 'the quietest light in the Hollow. Old light,' and the Oarsman's arm as 'gray and smooth and not quite the right color for anything alive' — strangeness rendered tactile and lovely before the horror (the withdrawing Current, Marl's story, the Tartar's dead cold) lands.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening beats — Glim reading the air temperature, checking the glow-rat candle, Leaf's rhythmic heat-stone pressing 'no one taught her,' the sentinel candle check — are pure world-maintenance rituals performed by someone who 'stopped being surprised' by them, well before any plot demand (the Surfacing call, the wrongness in the left tunnel) intrudes.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'CorpoNations,' 'Exclusion Economy,' 'Downward Expansion,' 'the Mission,' 'Channeler,' and 'covenant' are dropped in with the assumption of stranger-orientation but several arrive as clustered lecture rather than in-voice gloss — e.g. Vesh's line 'Before the sealing-off, when the deep still had a door to the surface's markets. Before the Exclusion Economy shut that door and called the shutting a law. Before the Downward Expansion drove the ones it shut out into the Works' stacks three proprietary-history terms back to back in a single breath of dialogue, functioning as compressed worldbuilding exposition rather than a natural Listener's aside.
checks.Fix: Break Vesh's history-recitation into smaller, separately-earned beats spread across the scene (each gloss triggered by something in the room or a Brave's question) rather than delivering the Exclusion Economy and Downward Expansion as a rapid-fire, unbroken litany.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: The acronym GLMZ is not present, but other acronyms/initialisms appear bare and unglossed at first use, e.g. the surface entity introduced only as 'the Mission' with no expansion, and 'the One Word'/'the Second Word' treated as established terms rather than glossed abbreviations — more clearly, no acronym in the text (such terms as they exist) is ever preceded by a spelled-out full term rendered in-voice before its short form is used.
checks.Fix: Introduce each institutional shorthand (e.g., 'the Mission') the first time it appears with an in-voice gloss of the full term it stands for before using the short form again.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: Sorrel juggling the too-hot meat strip Leaf hands him, and 'He understood the joke only later, laughing about it with Sorrel. That was the point' — a small, warm, unguarded human beat before he re-armors into duty; reinforced by Knuckle's remembered gesture and the crying-without-sound fragment, which flash genuine vulnerability before Glim returns to Brave discipline.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The node ends on an unresolved, actively suspenseful plot beat — the Oarsman inexplicably stopping mid-crossing, waiting for an unspecified additional payment — rather than a quiet gesture past the story's resolution; the final lines even gesture forward to plot logistics ('A new Fare. The Oarsman, waiting. The far bank behind him and the near bank ahead') instead of landing a settled emotional note.
checks.Fix: Resolve the crossing (let him land or clearly choose not to) and close instead on one small, concrete gesture — a candle checked, a name unsaid, a hand pressed to stone — that carries the accumulated cost without opening a new mystery.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: Details like Knuckle's hand-on-head gesture (echoed exactly when Knuckle repeats it years later), the pale face on a cord glimpsed in the Oarsman's basin, and Vesh's silence-piece 'I won't need it where I'm going' all read as complete, comprehensible beats on first pass but visibly accrue meaning once the reader knows the ending (Vesh's death, the unresolved origin-mystery, the final triple Fare) — none of them block understanding if missed, since each is glossed in-scene (e.g., 'the same gesture... that had lived all these years in the nerves of his crown').

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The excerpt reads as a fully realized, self-consistent story with its own vocabulary (Oarsman, Fare, Tartar, Underclan) that is patiently explained through grounded sensory scenes (candle-reading, the heat-stone rhythm, the Oarsman's arm as bar) rather than exposition dumps; new-reader orientation is achieved through scene-embedded clarification, not structural rewrites.
